title: DebtRecalled.v1
description: Payload of the DebtRecalled event (A§23). Emitted by agency-service — the single producer (A§7.2) — when a placement reaches RECALLED and the debt is back under bank control (A§5.12, D§12). Published on `collections.agency` keyed by `placementId` (A§23/§25), so it is ordered behind the DebtPlaced it terminates. Releases the A§11.6 mutual-exclusion lock: once legal-service has consumed this event the account becomes eligible for legal referral again (SVC-10), which is why the recall is a published fact rather than an internal status change. Rides the A§24 envelope; a breaking change ships as DebtRecalled.v2 (D§29).

placementId.description: Platform identifier of the recalled placement — the same value as the DebtPlaced it ends. Equal to the envelope `aggregateId` and the Kafka partition key (A§23).

agencyId.description: Platform identifier of the agency the debt is recalled from. Repeated from the placement so agency performance consumers need no prior state.

accountId.description: Platform identifier of the recalled account — the key on which the 'no active placement' condition is re-evaluated (A§11.6).

caseId.description: Platform identifier of the case the placement belonged to, so the recall lands as a case activity on the right case.

recalledAt.description: When the recall became effective with the agency (the business fact), RFC3339 UTC with a `Z` offset. Always on or after the matching `placedAt`.

reason.description: Why the debt was recalled. Open SCREAMING_SNAKE vocabulary rather than a closed enum: recall reasons are commercially and operationally driven (agency performance, customer dispute, legal escalation, end of placement term) and grow without changing what the event means. Required — an unexplained recall is not auditable (D§3.6).
